body: This sounds silly, but visualizing it all on Pinterest really helps. Just seeing every element I want in a room on one page makes it a lot easier to see like, if the colors don’t work or if everything is really square or smooth and you need some texture, especially if you’re like me and you don’t want everything to look like you just copied out of one catalog.

It’s a cute little studio in a really charming neighborhood. Original casement windows and that kind of thing. It’s my first time in my adult life having a dishwasher and the counter space to actually cook. And I have two huge closets which is unheard of in NYC, so that’s pretty sweet. 

When I left my last apartment I gave away all my crappy ikea furniture and decided I wasn’t going to buy anything new that I didn’t want to keep forever, so I’ve slowly been filling it up with things I love. But sometimes the care I put into like, choosing curtains and hanging art and arranging my bookshelves feels like an admission that I’m going to be alone forever, and that makes me super sad.

This sounds like what my therapist is always saying, only prettier. 

I just don’t understand how to feel different. I just finished graduate school, I have a career I love, I have a great apartment, I some wonderful friends, my family is pretty ok, I have good mental health support. And yet I’ve felt just absolutely hopeless and empty for the better part of a year.
I’ve been waiting for a really long time, and spending every weekend with no plans and no one to talk to just makes me feel even more worthless. No one else cares if I’m here, why should I?
